newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SOCCER-BRAZIL FIRE 10 GOALS PAST BELGIUM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL FIRE 10 GOALS PAST BELGIUM.

text.p: Favourites Brazil overwhelmed Belgium 10-0 in the world youth soccer championship on Wednesday to take their goal tally in the tournament to a remarkable 25 goals from six games.
Alex de Souza scored a hattrick as the South Americans, who thrashed South Korea 10-3 on Sunday, clinched the second-round victory with ease.
Adailton Martins, who hit six goals against Korea, contributed one goal to the scoring feast and now has 10 for the tournament.
"It was a game that was never a game," said Belgian coach Ariel Jacobs. "Even from the first minute, we could never reach the height of the Brazilians. We were running behind them.
"We just had too much respect for the Brazilians and we gave them too much space."
Brazil went ahead in the fourth minute with a goal from Alvaro and never looked back. They were 4-0 up by halftime.
In the quarter-finals the Brazilians now face the winner of Thursday's game between England and Argentina, while another South American side, Uruguay, have also reached the last eight.
Uruguay beat the United States 3-0, scoring all the goals in the first half, two from striker Marcelo Zalayeta. France also made the last eight with a 1-0 victory over Mexico.
But the real drama of the evening came in the final game as Ireland defeated Morocco with a golden goal in the fifth minute of extra time from Damien Duff.
